protocol.instrument: in-process std/time around the timed passes; per-iter ns = total_ns / timed_iters; median of 5 process runs, interleaved across all ports (run 1 of each, run 2 of each, ...)
protocol.workload: rule i: p_i += vx over 10k f64 rows; identical 9-column schema (vx, p1..p8) in every port; rules are unconstrained (no depends_on) and legally fusible per koru 690_202/690_044 (disjoint write sets, shared read column)

series.rf_stripe_N: N standing [name]d rules fired through std/store:stripe once per frame. Emitted pass structure (read before timing): __store_stripe_<s> chains N per-rule qsweeps in topo order (store.kz:3371 'naive per-rule passes; fusion is a later, semantics-preserving scheduling change'); each qsweep is a while loop whose per-row visit loads ALL 9 columns, resolves the handle twice, and dispatches a centralized 9-value __store_write envelope. N corpus passes per frame, each on the standing-rule row machinery. The stripe_N oracle includes each rule's one root-position firing (690_200).
series.rf_sweeps_N: the same N rule bodies as N separate imperative sweeps, each timed in its own block (a sweep has no completion branch); runner sums the N total_ns lines. N corpus passes per frame on the sweep machinery: for (0..len) loop, per row one __store_envwrite + one announce.
series.rf_fused_N: the same N rule bodies hand-fused into ONE sweep whose stored block writes all N columns per row (multi-column write, koru 690_118/125). ONE corpus pass per frame; per row N __store_envwrite + N announce calls. rf_fused_1 is program-identical to rf_sweeps_1 (same-measurement control: its delta vs rf_sweeps_1 is the noise band under this load).

protocol.oracle: checksum line matched per-port expected file on every process run; no port excluded
